failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'What is the actual setting and filming location of the 2004 horror film R-Point, and where exactly is Bokor Hill Station located in relation to Povokvil Waterfalls in Cambodia?' Hop 3 query: 'What is the correct setting location for the 2004 horror film R-Point, where was it filmed, and what is the geographical relationship between the filming locations and Povokvil Waterfalls?' Both queries ask essentially the same compound question about R-Point's setting, filming location, and geographical relationship to Povokvil Waterfalls. Hop 2 retrieval returned the same 3 core documents (Bokor Hill Station, Povokvil Waterfalls, R-Point) that hop 1 had already provided, and hop 3 retrieval again returned these same documents.

failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'What is the actual setting and filming location of the 2004 horror film R-Point, and where exactly is Bokor Hill Station located in relation to Povokvil Waterfalls in Cambodia?' Hop 3 query: 'What is the correct setting location for the 2004 horror film R-Point, where was it filmed, and what is the geographical relationship between the filming locations and Povokvil Waterfalls?' Both queries are natural-language questions bundling multiple targets: (1) the setting location, (2) filming locations, and (3) geographical relationships. These compound multi-part formulations make it difficult for the retriever to target specific entities.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: After hop 2, the solver received passages about 'Amityville Death House' (a 2015 horror film), 'Kodikuthimala' (a hill station in India), and 'City of Ghosts' (a 2002 film). None of these are relevant to verifying claims about R-Point. After hop 3, the solver received passages about '10%: What Makes a Hero?', 'A Daughter of the Gods', 'My Son, My Son, What Have Ye Done?', 'Stanley Film Festival', 'List of Saint Seiya films', 'The Dream', 'We Are What We Are', and 'List of horror films set in academic institutions' - all clearly irrelevant to the R-Point claim. The queries generated show the solver did not filter out this noise and continued requesting essentially the same information.
